title: SpecPIM: Accelerating Speculative Inference on PIM-Enabled System via Architecture-Dataflow Co-Exploration
problem: LLM inference efficiency is limited by token dependency in autoregressive decoding. Speculative inference introduces variable resource demands due to different computation patterns in draft token generation versus verification, preventing efficient system utilization.
motivation: Speculative inference promises significant efficiency gains for LLM inference, but variable resource demands from heterogeneous model sizes prevent current systems from fully realizing the acceleration potential.
method: SpecPIM co-explores architecture design and dataflow optimization on PIM-enabled systems to adapt to variable resource demands in speculative inference. The approach optimizes computation placement and data movement for both small-model draft token generation and large-model verification stages within processing-in-memory architectures.
key_novelty: Architecture-dataflow co-exploration methodology that dynamically adapts PIM systems to variable resource demands across different speculative inference stages.
contributions: PIM-based acceleration framework for speculative inference
Architecture-dataflow co-design methodology for heterogeneous computation patterns
System design approach to realize full acceleration potential despite variable resource demands
Evaluation showing efficiency gains from matched architecture-dataflow optimization
limitations: Experimental evaluation details, specific baseline comparisons, and practical scalability constraints not discussed in abstract.
primary_theme: speculative inference acceleration via PIM architecture-dataflow codesign
